name: Dynamic Programming
description: Dynamic programming (DP) solves problems by breaking them into overlapping subproblems, solving each once, and storing the results. It is ideal for optimization problems with optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems.
how_to_identify: The problem asks for the count / maximum / minimum / best way and can be decomposed into smaller versions of itself with overlapping states.
template: Define the state (what describes a subproblem). Write a recurrence connecting larger states to smaller ones. Choose filling order top-down (memoized recursion) or bottom-up (tabular).
time_complexity: Number of states × cost to compute each state
space_complexity: Depends on the number of states; often reducible to O(1) or O(N) via rolling arrays
common_mistakes: Writing the recurrence without a clear base case.
Confusing greedy with DP when a local choice is not globally optimal.
Missing the memoization step, leaving exponential time.
